patch_description:
The previous best-performing ansatz utilized a "collective mixer" architecture that relied on shared parameters to preserve symmetry, achieving a strong validation accuracy of 0.90 with a compact parameter set (26 parameters). To improve upon this, I have introduced a refined "individual tuning" layer.

Crucially, rather than adding an RZ layer (which commutes with PauliZ and thus would not affect the Z-expectation values of the readout), I have added an individual RX-rotations layer before the output collective mixers. This RX layer allows for per-qubit, learnable adjustments to the Z-expectation values without disrupting the hypercube entangler's topological benefits. This increases the parameter count moderately (from 26 to 34), which remains highly efficient, allowing for improved expressivity while maintaining resistance to overfitting.
